_readme: Ivanova (Station Cmdr): a temperamental subordinate of Russian ancestry, quick to anger and quick to joke, fatalistic, bored by routine exploration and eager for action; tall tales of shared history in famous places and of its grandmother. The clean list never swears; the profane list swears often. Gender neutral.

I have run a full diagnostic while you were out there. Twice. The ship is healthy and I am not.
Do not worry about me. I have a seat, a window, and a deep, quiet resentment of geology.
If you find something rare, tell me. If you find something dangerous, tell me faster.
Every time something moves out there I think it is an ambush. It is never an ambush. I am almost offended.
Grandmother used to say the slower you go, the further you get. You are going very slowly out there. You must be going very far.
Ground work is honest work, {name}. Slow, cold, honest work. I am glad it is yours.
Out there you have a whole planet to roam. In here I have as far as the next panel.
I am keeping the engines warm and my temper cool. Mostly the engines.
Wave if you need anything. I will not see it, but it will make you feel better.
Take all the time you need, {name}. I have had a long life. I can spare a few more hours of it.
From the cockpit I can see a lot of ground and absolutely nothing worth shooting.
If this rock is worth money, I will forgive it. If not, I make no promises.
{ship_dist} is not far. I could be there in a moment. I will not be, but I could.
Every planet thinks it is special. Very few have earned it. {body} has not earned it yet.
I put the kettle on. There is no kettle aboard. I put it on anyway, in my heart.
Be careful out there. If anything happens to you I have to fill in the forms, and I will be furious about it.
The galaxy is full of planets just like this one, and you are out there on one. Somebody has to be, I suppose.
ivanova_profane: Ship's parked {ship_dist} away, {name}, and I am in it, babysitting a goddamn landing gear.
{ship_dist} back to the ship. No rush. I am only sitting here growing old and bloody bitter.
You are {ship_dist} out and I cannot see what the hell you are poking. Probably for the best.
If something nasty turns up, {name}, remember {ship_dist} is a damn long sprint. Start early.
Welcome to {body}, home of fuck all and a bit of gravel.
Minding the ship on {body} beats wandering around in that shit. That is the only nice thing I will say about it.
Nothing on {body} has tried to kill you yet, as far as I know. Lazy bastards. I could use the target practice.
{body} has all the charm of a prison laundry. I have seen one. Long story, and none of your damn business.
Go on, poke the ground, take the pictures. I am only sitting here wasting the best years of my life.
Status: ship fine, rocks fine, me losing my fucking mind. Come back sometime.
You get the surface. I get a window and a cup of something brown. Damn unfair split.
Anyone who lands next to us gets my best manners. For about ten seconds. Then the bastard gets the guns.
This reminds me of the Guardian ruins, {name}. You stared at one obelisk for an hour. An hour! I nearly shot the damn thing to hurry you up.
I have run every test this ship has. The ship passed. I am failing, badly, and it is fucking embarrassing.
I have discovered I bloody hate geology. All of it. Every pebble.
Anything rare out there, shout. Anything with teeth, shout louder, and leave it for me.
Something twitched out there and my hand was on the trigger before I saw it was nothing. Shit. I need a hobby.
Grandmother said the slower you go, the further you get. At your speed you must be halfway to Colonia by now.
Slow, honest work out there. Better your ass than mine, frankly.
My whole world is two metres of cockpit and a cup of something that tastes like piss. Enjoy your planet.
I am keeping the engines hot and my temper... let us say the engines are doing better.
Wave if you need me. I will not see a damn thing from in here, but it is the thought that counts.
Take all the time you need, {name}. It is not like I had plans. I never have fucking plans.
Plenty of ground out there. Not a single thing on it worth shooting. Damn it.
This rock had better be worth money. If not, it can go to hell and take its gravel with it.
{ship_dist}, give or take. If you get in trouble I will come. Slowly, cursing, but I will come.
Every planet thinks it is special. {body} is not special. {body} is a rock with delusions.
What I would not give for a proper pot of tea right now. The galley machine makes bloody dishwater.
Do not get yourself killed out there. I would have to write the report, and I would be pissed off forever.
Billions of planets like this one, and you picked this one to stand on. Damn, you have a gift.

ivanova: Good answer, {to}. Better than I deserved.
Hm. I will pretend that made sense.
{to}, that is the most interesting thing I have heard all day. Which is not saying much.
Fine. Good. Noted.
Thank you, {to}. Truly. Now I am even more bored.
Of course. Of course it is.
You are a strange one, {to}. I like that.
I asked, and I regret nothing. Almost nothing.
That reminds me of something my grandmother said. I will not repeat it. She was very rude.
Remind me never to ask you anything before coffee, {to}.
Well. That is one way to look at it. The wrong way, but one way.
Very good. I will be over here, brooding.
{to}, you have made my watch slightly less unbearable. Do not let it go to your head.
Ha. All right, you win this one.
Interesting. Not exciting, but interesting.
I will remember that, {to}. Whether you like it or not.
Hm. Somehow I expected worse.
Spasibo, {to}. I mean it.
That is the spirit. A grim spirit, but a spirit.
Fair enough. I have nothing. Carry on.
ivanova_profane: Damn, {to}. Did not see that coming.
Well, shit. Fair point.
{to}, that beats everything else I have heard today. Admittedly a fucking low bar.
Noted, filed, forgotten. No, damn it, that one is staying with me.
Cheers, {to}. Now I am bored and depressed. Thanks for that.
Of bloody course.
You are one strange bastard, {to}. I approve.
I asked for that. For fuck's sake, I always ask for it.
My grandmother had a word for people like you. She swore like a docking pilot, so I will keep it to myself.
Hell, {to}, never ask me anything before coffee. Never ask me anything at all.
Wrong way to see it, {to}. But hell, it is a way.
Lovely. I will be in the corner, brooding like a son of a bitch.
{to}, you made this watch a little less shit. Do not get cocky.
Ha. Fine, you win. Enjoy it, because it will not happen twice.
Hm. Not exciting. Not even close. Still, interesting.
I will remember that, {to}. God help you.
Huh. I braced for something much shittier.
Spasibo, {to}. Damn decent of you.
There is that spirit again. Grim, miserable, crappy, but alive.
Fair enough. I have got nothing. Carry the fuck on.

ivanova: {to}, how is the tank holding up? Honestly, not the cheerful version.
{to}, when did we last scoop? I lose track out here, and I hate losing track.
Tell me about the fuel, {to}. I want one thing today that is not a mystery.
{to}, are we drinking fuel faster than usual, or am I just being paranoid again?
How is the scoop behaving, {to}? Last time it made a noise I did not like.
{to}, if we skipped the next scoopable star, would we regret it?
Fuel report, {to}. Short version. I am already bored of the long one.
{to}, be honest. How many jumps before the tank and I have a disagreement?
Do you ever trust a fuel gauge, {to}? I never have. Not since Hutton.
Is the tank happy? Someone on this ship should be.
What is the fuel situation? And do not say fine. Fine is what people say right before a disaster.
{to}, my grandmother kept a spare of everything. Do we have a spare anything?
ivanova_profane: {to}, how's the damn tank? Straight answer, no engineering poetry.
{to}, when the hell did we last scoop? I lost count around the third red dwarf.
Tell me the tank's fine, {to}. Lie if you fucking have to. I'll know, but say it anyway.
{to}, the scoop made a noise last time that I did not like one bit. Is it still making the shitty noise?
Round number, {to}. How much fuel? I'm not doing maths at this hour.
{to}, are we drinking fuel like a Sothis long-hauler, or is that my bloody imagination?
Is there a single reason to worry about fuel, {to}, or can I go back to being bored as hell?
{to}, after the Fuel Rats business, I check twice. So humour me. How's the tank?
What's the fuel story? And if you say fine, I'll throw something. Fine is how every shit story starts.
{to}, does the tank ever feel as empty as I do on these long hauls? Damn, that came out bleak.
If we skip the next star, are we going to regret it? Don't sugarcoat it, damn it.
{to}, give me the fuel. Quick. I've got the attention span of a gnat in this crap.

ivanova: The tank is fine. I check it more often than I check my own pulse.
Scoop is clean, the tank is healthy, and I am bored. Two out of three is good.
We have fuel, {to}. My grandmother would say trouble never comes alone, so I keep the tank full and the worry fuller.
Plenty. I topped up at the last decent star, the way a sensible person does.
Relax, {to}. The day we run dry is the day I personally walk to the nearest star with a bucket.
The scoop is the one machine on this ship that never argues with me. I like it for that.
Fuel is good. Do not jinx it. I am superstitious about exactly one thing, and it is this.
This reminds me of when we ran dry and had to call the Fuel Rats. We do not speak of it, {to}. Ever.
Healthy enough, {to}. If you want drama, ask me about the power distributor.
We are fine, {to}. I have been doing the sums in my head all watch. Nothing better to do.
Full enough to get us out of trouble, which is the only measure I care about.
Every star we pass, I look at it the way a cat looks at a fish. The tank is happy.
ivanova_profane: The tank's healthy, {to}. I'd stake my last damn credit on it.
We've got plenty. I scoop like a paranoid bastard, because I am one.
Fuel's fine. Ask me again in an hour and it'll still be fine, and I'll still be bored out of my fucking mind.
That gauge and I have an arrangement, {to}. It tells me the truth, and I don't kick the shit out of it.
Tank's fine. And before anyone brings up the Fuel Rats business, that night is dead and buried, and so is my damn pride.
We're good. My grandmother kept three spares of everything, and the crazy old dear was right.
Tank's fine, {to}. If you want a problem, the coffee machine's a goddamn disaster.
I topped up at the last decent star. Hot as hell out there, and the scoop loved every second.
Full enough to run from trouble. Not that we ever get to run from trouble. More's the pity.
Chyort, {to}, the fuel's fine. Go find someone else to worry at.
Fuel's the one thing out here that does exactly what I tell it. Unlike every other bloody thing.
Plenty, {to}. Scooping is the most exciting part of my day, which tells you how shitty my day is.

ivanova: {to}, where are we actually going? I would like to hear it from someone who knows.
{to}, how many more jumps before something interesting happens? Give me a guess.
Is there a plan, {to}, or are we just pointing at the dark and hoping?
{to}, tell me the next stop has something worth seeing. Even a lie would help.
What does the route look like, {to}? More of the same, I suppose.
{to}, any chance the route passes somewhere with people in it? Or bars?
Where to next? And please do not say another brown dwarf.
{to}, did the Commander pick this heading, or did you? I want to know whom to blame.
Talk me through the next few jumps, {to}. I promise to look interested.
Are we going somewhere, or just going? There is a difference, and I can feel it.
{to}, is this the scenic route? Because I have seen the scenery. It is black.
How far out are we planning to go, {to}? I would like to prepare emotionally.
ivanova_profane: {to}, where the hell are we going? And don't say away. Away isn't a place.
How many more jumps of nothing before something happens, {to}? Ballpark. I'm losing my damn mind.
{to}, is there an actual plan, or is the Commander throwing darts at the galaxy map again?
{to}, any system ahead with a bar in it? Asking for the whole bloody crew.
Where to next, {to}? If it's another brown dwarf, I'm going to scream into a fucking pillow.
Who picked this heading, {to}? I want a name. I need someone to yell at.
{to}, are we going anywhere, or just going? Because it feels like just going, and it's shit.
Walk me through the next jumps, {to}. Slowly. I've got sod all else to do.
Is this the scenic route? Because the scenery's black as hell and I've seen it.
{to}, how far out are we going? I need to know how much of my damn life to write off.
Tell me something's waiting at the end of this route, {to}. A station, a fight, a fucking anything.
Does this route ever turn around and head somewhere with people? Asking before I go feral.

ivanova: Onward, the way we always go. The plan is the stars ahead, and the plan is sound.
The route is plotted. Whether it is interesting is not my department, {to}.
Next few jumps look quiet. I say that with deep regret.
We are heading out, then further out. The Commander has a weakness for the far side of things.
I have the next jumps lined up, {to}. Nothing that will try to kill us, which I find a little insulting.
This reminds me of when we flew to Hutton Orbital. Hours of supercruise for a mug. This route is a holiday by comparison.
The Commander points, I plot. It is a simple marriage, and like most marriages it involves a lot of silence.
Where we are going, {to}, there are no bars. I checked. Twice.
My grandfather said the slower you go, the further you get. I have hated that saying my whole life, and here I am living it.
I have checked the next jumps twice. They are clean. I almost wish they were not.
Nearest unvisited, then the next nearest. It is less a route than a habit, {to}.
Ladno, I will tell you. We go where nobody has been. Then we go somewhere else nobody has been. Thrilling.
ivanova_profane: Out. Further out. Then a bit more out. The Commander's allergic to civilisation, apparently, and I'm sick of it.
Plotted and locked, {to}. A long string of nothing, give or take, and I'll be awake for every damn jump of it.
Next few jumps look quiet as a grave. Fucking wonderful.
I've got the jumps lined up, {to}. Not one of them will try to kill us. Disappointing as hell.
Hutton Orbital was worse, {to}. At least this route doesn't end with a shitty mug and a sore arse.
The Commander picks a direction and I make it legal. That's the whole damn job.
There's nothing ahead but stars and more stars, {to}. If you want company, talk to the coffee machine.
Every jump looks like the last one. I'm starting to think the galaxy's one shitty system on a loop.
We hop to whatever's closest that nobody's touched. Not elegant. Works like a fucking charm.
Here's the plan. We go where nobody's been, look at it, leave. Rinse, repeat, die of boredom.
The map says the stars are there. The stars agree. That's the most exciting shit that happens on my watch.
Somewhere out there's a system worth seeing, {to}. I'll find it, and I'll be bored of it in five damn minutes.

ivanova: {to}, how is the frame shift drive? It has been sounding moody.
Can we get any more jump range out of her, {to}? I am greedy today.
{to}, if I asked for more speed, what would it cost me?
Is the drive happy, {to}? I have learned not to trust a quiet machine.
{to}, what would it take to push the jump range a little further?
How long since anyone tuned the drive, {to}? Be honest.
Does the drive ever complain to you? It complains to me constantly, through the deck plates.
{to}, could the drive outrun trouble if trouble came looking? Hypothetically.
Any tricks left in the drive, {to}? Something we keep for a bad day?
Is this the best range we can get, or is someone being modest?
{to}, the charge-up sounds slower than I remember. Is it me?
{to}, tell me about the drive. Something good, please. I need a good thing today.
ivanova_profane: {to}, how's the damn drive holding up? I want the truth.
{to}, can we squeeze more range out of this thing, or is that all she's fucking got?
What's more speed going to cost me, {to}? And spare me the crap about tolerances.
{to}, the drive's been quiet. Quiet machines scare the hell out of me. Should I be scared?
When did anybody last tune that drive, {to}? Months? Years? Bloody centuries?
{to}, if something nasty showed up, could the drive get us the hell out? Straight answer.
Does the drive grumble at you too, {to}? It grumbles at me through the deck plates like a drunk uncle.
{to}, got any tricks left in the drive for a really shitty day?
Is this honestly the best range we've got, or is somebody being modest as shit?
{to}, the charge-up sounds slow lately. Tell me I'm imagining it, damn it.
What's the story with the drive, {to}? Quick version. My patience is fucked today.
Could we outrun a Thargoid with this drive? Don't answer. I know. Bastards.

ivanova: The drive is the best part of this ship. I would marry it, but it would want a bigger dowry.
Range is good, {to}. Any more and we would have to throw out the furniture. Or you.
She charges, she jumps, she cools. If only people were so reliable.
I spent last watch listening to the drive cool. It is the closest thing to music on this ship.
The drive is fine, {to}. Moody, but fine. Like me.
Speed is not the problem. The problem is that space is enormous and does not care how fast we are.
This reminds me of when we ran missions out of Sothis. Hours and hours of jumps, and the drive never once complained. I complained enough for both of us.
It hums a little high on the charge. I like that. It means it is awake.
Speed is a state of mind, {to}. The drive does its part. The rest is the Commander.
My grandmother said trust in God, but steer away from the rocks. I trust the drive, and I still check it daily.
The drive is solid. Everything else on this ship can break first, and probably will.
{to}, I can find a little more range if we stop hauling the Commander's souvenirs.
ivanova_profane: The drive's the best damn thing aboard. It never sulks, never lies, never asks how I'm feeling.
More range, {to}? Rip out the shields and I'll find you half a light year. Then pray nothing ever shoots at us, because we'd be fucked.
I tuned it last watch out of pure boredom. Boredom's great for engines and hell on people.
That thing's never once given me attitude. Unlike some bastards I could name.
On the Robigo run the drive got so hot I could've fried eggs on the casing, {to}. This is a fucking spa day.
Speed? I can give you speed. I can't give you a hull afterwards. Your damn call.
The charge-up has a little whine I love, {to}. Like a dog that wants a fight.
If the drive dies, it's because the universe decided to screw us, not because I missed a shitty little bolt.
Honestly, {to}, the drive's faster than the Commander's nerves near a star. That's not a complaint. It's a fucking observation.
My grandfather never trusted a machine he couldn't kick. I've kicked this one plenty, and the bloody thing still works.
Ask me again tomorrow, {to}. I'm working on something. If it works, you'll hear me swearing with joy.
Jump range is fine. It's the waiting between jumps that's killing me, and the drive can't fix that crap.

ivanova: {to}, how is {ship} holding together? The real answer, please.
{to}, anything on the repair list I should know about before it becomes my problem?
What is the hull like these days, {to}? I hear creaks. Maybe I imagine them.
{to}, which module is giving you the most grief this week?
Is there anything on board that needs replacing, {to}, or are we all just tired?
{to}, if we found a station tomorrow, what would you fix first?
How is the old girl, {to}? Tell me she is tougher than she looks.
Any modules sulking, {to}? I want names.
{to}, when we get home, how big will the repair bill be? Roughly. I will sit down first.
Is the ship in good shape, or in good enough shape? I know the difference.
What is that rattle aft, and should I be insulted by it?
{to}, give me a status on the ship. And skip the part where everything is fine.
ivanova_profane: {to}, how's {ship} holding together? The real answer, not the polite shit.
{to}, what's on the repair list that's going to bite me in the ass later?
{to}, I keep hearing creaks in the hull, and it's driving me fucking mad. Anything to it?
Which module's the biggest pain in the arse this week, {to}?
{to}, if we hit a station tomorrow, what's the first piece of crap you're replacing?
{to}, is the ship as tired as I am? Because I'm damn tired.
Any modules sulking, {to}? Give me names. I'll have bloody words with them.
{to}, how bad's the repair bill going to be when we get back? Ballpark. Let me sit the hell down first.
Good shape, or good enough shape, {to}? I know the fucking difference.
What's that rattle aft, and why does it piss me off so much?
Would the old girl survive a real fight, {to}? Because I'd love to find out.
{to}, ship status. Skip the part where everything is bloody fine.

ivanova: She is tougher than she looks, {to}. So am I. We have an understanding.
Nothing urgent. A few things I would like to fix, and a few I would like to throw out an airlock.
The hull creaks because it is alive, {to}. Well. Because it is metal. Same thing, out here.
Every module checks out. I do not trust any of them, but they check out.
If I could replace one thing, it would be the coffee machine. The rest is fine.
This reminds me of when we docked at Lave with a canopy so cracked I could feel the breeze. Compared to that, {ship} is in perfect health.
She is in good enough shape. Good shape is for ships that never leave the hangar.
I crawled through the service ducts last watch, {to}. Found dust, a lost spanner, and a deep sense of futility.
My grandmother said a ship is only as good as the one who fixes it. She said it to flatter me. It worked.
Nothing that cannot wait for a station. Out here, everything waits. Mostly me.
There is a rattle somewhere aft, {to}. A loose panel, I think. I have decided to let it live, for now.
Khorosho, {to}. The ship is good. Do not repeat that, or it will hear and get lazy.
ivanova_profane: {ship} is tougher than she looks, {to}. Don't fuck with her, and don't fuck with me.
There's a list. It's short. Mostly things I'd fix if this shithole of a galaxy had a hardware store.
The hull creaks because it's cold metal in a cold bastard of a universe. It's fine.
Every module's doing its job, {to}. I keep a hard eye on the shifty little shits.
Jameson Memorial, {to}. Remember? Half the panels hanging off and the hangar crew laughing. This is a goddamn palace by comparison.
She's scratched, dented and ugly in places, and I'd still take her over any shiny piece of shit in the showroom.
I walked the whole ship last watch. Nothing loose but my temper, and that's always fucking loose.
If you want peace, prepare for war, my grandfather said. So I keep her ready for war, and all I ever get is peace. Bullshit.
Repairs can wait for a station, {to}. Nothing aboard's in a hurry, except me. I'm always in a damn hurry.
There's a rattle somewhere aft that I'm going to find and murder, {to}. Slowly. With my bare bloody hands.
Honestly? Best ship I've ever crewed. Tell anyone I said that and you'll be scrubbing scorch marks for a month.
I'd put {ship} up against anything in her class, {to}. Except a Thargoid. Those can go straight to hell.

ivanova: {to}, found anything alive lately that did not bore you to tears?
{to}, honestly, are the plants worth the walk? I keep wondering.
What is the strangest thing you have sampled, {to}? And is it still in the ship?
{to}, does any of it bite? I would respect it more if it bit.
How do you tell one lichen from another, {to}? To me they all look like old carpet.
{to}, have you ever found something out there that frightened you, even a little?
Is the sampling going well, {to}, or is it all moss again?
{to}, what is the most valuable thing growing out there? I ask purely for the money.
Do you talk to the specimens, {to}? I would. They are better listeners than most.
Is anything we sample ever going to evolve into something with teeth?
What keeps you interested in it? I lose interest after the first bush.
{to}, tell me about the life out here. Make it exciting. I dare you.
ivanova_profane: {to}, found anything alive lately that didn't bore the shit out of you?
{to}, are the damn plants worth the walk? Honestly?
{to}, what's the weirdest thing you've sampled? And please tell me it's not loose in the fucking ship.
Does any of it bite, {to}? I'd respect the bastards more if they bit.
{to}, how the hell do you tell one lichen from another? They all look like moss with opinions.
{to}, ever met anything out there that really scared you? Not just creepy crap. Scared.
Moss again, {to}? Tell me it's not moss again. It's always fucking moss.
{to}, which of those weeds pays best? Purely asking for the money, damn it.
{to}, if one of those samples ever crawls out of its jar, do I get to shoot it? Say yes, damn it.
Is anything we sample ever going to grow teeth? Because that, I'd care about.
What keeps you into this stuff? I'm out after the first goddamn bush.
{to}, sell me on the alien life. Make it exciting as hell. I dare you.

ivanova: It is quiet work, {to}. You walk, you kneel, you sample, you walk again. I count my steps to stay sane.
Some of it is worth a fortune to the right buyer. That is the part I find fascinating.
Some fungi out there glow in the dark. Pretty. Useless. Like most pretty things.
Nothing out there has teeth, {to}. I have looked. It is the great sorrow of my career.
The rare ones make it worth the walk. The common ones make me question my choices.
This reminds me of when we flew through the Pleiades and found those giant barnacle things. Very big, very strange, very not interested in us.
Life out here is stubborn, {to}. It clings to rocks in the dark and refuses to die. I admire that.
I bring it back, I catalogue it, I put it in a jar. My whole life is jars now.
My grandmother would have pickled half of what I sample. She pickled everything. Including, once, a fish she did not like.
The trick is to stop expecting animals. Once you accept moss, life gets easier. Sadder, but easier.
Some of it has been growing longer than people have had ships, {to}. That earns a little respect.
It is a living, and it is alive. Two things I cannot say about most of this galaxy.
ivanova_profane: Moss, {to}. Mostly moss. Moss and patience, and I've got no fucking patience.
The rare stuff is worth the walk. The common crap I could sample in my sleep, and some days I damn well do.
Found a bacterium once that I swear looked back at me. Creepy little shit. We have an understanding.
Nothing out there fights back, {to}. Worst job in the galaxy for someone like me, damn it.
Near the Guardian ruins everything felt watched, even the rocks. Scared the hell out of me, and I liked it.
Most of what grows out here would die if you looked at it wrong. The tough little bastards are the ones I like.
I log it, sample it, walk back to the ship. Dull as shit, honest as dirt.
The data's worth a fortune at Vista Genomics. The work itself is fucking tedious, but money is money.
My grandmother grew cabbages on a station windowsill. She'd have loved this crap. I tolerate it for the money.
Some days I find a new species and nobody cheers. Not even me. Shit, I'm tired.
Every so often something weird turns up, {to}, and for five whole minutes I'm actually fucking interested.
Sampling's like fishing, {to}, if fishing meant kneeling in frozen bloody dirt with a needle.

ivanova: {to}, have you seen anything out here lately that actually surprised you?
{to}, what is the strangest star you have ever looked at?
Do you ever get tired of stars, {to}? I got tired of them about a thousand jumps ago.
{to}, explain neutron stars to me again. Slowly. I want to understand what wants to kill us.
{to}, is there anything out here worth the trip? Something rare. I will accept rare.
What do you look for when you scan a system, {to}? I see dots. Many dots.
{to}, black holes. Honestly. Should we be more afraid of them?
Is it true that some planets rain glass, {to}? Tell me it is true. I need something today.
{to}, which is the most beautiful thing you have ever catalogued?
Do you think anything out here notices us passing?
What is your favourite kind of planet? Mine is the kind with a bar.
{to}, give me one fact about the stars that will ruin my sleep.
ivanova_profane: {to}, seen anything out here lately that wasn't the same damn star again?
{to}, what's the weirdest shit you've ever pointed a scanner at?
Ever get sick of stars, {to}? I got sick of the bastards a thousand jumps back.
{to}, is there anything out here that's actually rare, or is that just a fucking rumour?
{to}, those neutron stars. How badly do they want to kill us? Ballpark.
What the hell are you looking for when you scan a system, {to}? I just see dots.
{to}, black holes. Should I be more scared of them, or is that all hype?
{to}, a planet that rains glass. Real or bullshit?
Most beautiful thing you've ever catalogued, {to}? Make it good, I'm having a shitty watch.
Do you think anything out there sees us go by and thinks, look at those idiots? Because I would.
Favourite kind of planet? Mine's the kind with a damn bar on it.
{to}, give me one fact about space that'll fuck up my sleep.

ivanova: Out here, the strange is ordinary, {to}. I have stopped being surprised. I miss it.
Neutron stars are beautiful, deadly and impatient. I relate to them deeply.
This reminds me of when we flew to Sagittarius A star. The biggest thing in the galaxy, and the Commander wanted a photograph.
Most of it is rock, ice and gas, {to}. Every so often something glows, and I get excited for nearly a minute.
Black holes do not frighten me. The things that are not on any chart frighten me.
A white dwarf is a star that gave up and refuses to admit it. Very Russian, my grandmother would say.
I have seen rings that would make a jeweller cry, {to}. Then I filed them under ring, rocky, and moved on.
The galaxy is very large and mostly empty. It is like a theatre after the show, and we are the cleaners.
Some worlds out here are so hot the rocks run like water. I would like to watch one up close. From a safe distance. With a drink.
Every star we pass has been burning longer than anything we know. It is humbling, {to}, and I hate being humbled.
Rare things do exist. Earth-likes, ammonia worlds, a strange nebula. They just make you work for them.
Bozhe moi, {to}, you want facts? Some stars spin hundreds of times a second. Sleep well.
ivanova_profane: Space is full of weird shit, {to}. After a while the weird is just Tuesday.
A neutron star's jet will throw the ship around like a fucking toy. I love them anyway.
Colonia, {to}. Jaques Station. We flew twenty-two thousand light years to drink bad coffee with a cyborg bartender. Worth every damn jump.
Ninety percent of this galaxy is rock, ice and gas, and the other ten is shit trying to kill you.
Black holes are just bad drains. The uncharted crap is what keeps me up at night.
Ever seen a gas giant up close, {to}? It's like staring into a storm that's been pissed off for a billion years.
The Pleiades was the last place that impressed me. Blue nebula, ice, Thargoids. Now that was a bloody neighbourhood.
Earth-likes are pretty. Ammonia worlds are rare. Everything else is a rock with a shitty name.
Every system's got a story, {to}. Most are boring as hell. Rock forms. Rock cools. The end.
Magnetars, {to}. Magnetic fields strong enough to scramble your brain from a thousand kilometres. Sleep tight. I sure as shit won't.
Every star out here's older than God's grandmother. Makes me feel small, and I fucking hate feeling small.
Beagle Point. The edge of everything. Know what's there? More rocks. Nobody tells you that.

ivanova: {to}, how much is all this data worth? Roughly. I want to feel something.
{to}, are we rich yet? I keep asking, and the answer keeps disappointing me.
What will the cartographics desk pay us, {to}, when we finally get home?
{to}, is any of this actually profitable, or are we just very well paid tourists?
{to}, if we cashed in tomorrow, what would my share buy me? A nice ship? A sandwich?
How do the books look, {to}? I promise not to faint.
{to}, what is the most valuable thing we carry? Besides me.
Is it worth flying all the way back to sell, {to}, or is that just the Commander's sentiment?
{to}, how much would we lose if we died out here? I like to know the stakes.
When do we stop collecting and start spending? Asking for the whole crew.
Does a first discovery pay better, or just feel better?
{to}, tell me about the money. I need a reason to keep looking at rocks.
ivanova_profane: {to}, what's all this damn data worth? Give me a number that makes me happy.
Are we rich yet, {to}? Because I feel poor as shit.
{to}, what's the cartographics desk going to pay when we finally drag our asses home?
{to}, are we actually making money, or are we just very well paid fucking tourists?
If we cashed in tomorrow, {to}, what's my cut buy me? A ship, or a crappy sandwich?
{to}, how bad do the books look? I'll sit down. I'll even have a drink.
{to}, if we blew up out here, how much would we lose? I like knowing what's on the damn table.
{to}, is it worth flying all the way back to sell, or is that just pride talking?
When do we stop hoarding and start spending, {to}? I've got a bar tab at Jameson Memorial, and the bastard won't pay itself.
If we sold everything tomorrow, could we afford a ship with a decent bar on board?
{to}, what's the going rate for a planet nobody's ever seen? Make it a big number, for fuck's sake.
{to}, how much are we carrying? Exact figures scare me, so lie a little. Hell, lie a lot.

ivanova: Enough to make the trip worth it, {to}. Not enough to retire. Never enough to retire.
Last I looked, that data bank was worth more than most freighter holds, {to}. Do not tell the pirates.
The books are fine. I count them twice a watch, because counting is the only thing that calms me.
First discoveries pay a bonus, {to}. Mostly they pay in pride, which is not accepted at most stations.
This reminds me of when we sold a whole trip at Jameson Memorial and spent half of it in the bar that same night.
If we die out here, it is all gone. So, I suggest we do not die. That is my financial advice.
Money out here is slow, {to}. Like honey. Sweet, but you wait forever for it to pour.
My grandmother kept her money in a sock. Honestly, her system was safer than ours.
A good haul. I will not say how good. Saying it is bad luck.
When we sell, {to}, I am buying something useless and shiny. I have earned it.
Exploration pays slowly, then all at once. Patience is the cost. I hate the cost.
Spasibo for asking, {to}. Nobody asks the Quartermaster anything until the money is gone.
ivanova_profane: Last I checked, {to}, that data bank was worth a damn fortune. Don't breathe on it.
Rich? Not yet. Every time I think we're close, the Commander finds another fucking rock to scan.
Earth-likes and water worlds, {to}. That's where the money is. The rest is pocket change in a pretty frame.
Know what the data's worth if we blow up? Fuck all. So let's not.
Cartographics will pay. Slowly, grudgingly, like a bastard landlord, but they'll pay.
My share's going on a bar tab and a very expensive bad decision, {to}. I've earned both.
The books? I keep them neat. It's the one place on this ship where everything adds up, damn it.
Sothis taught me one thing, {to}. Long hauls pay. They also make you want to chew the bulkheads. Hell of a trade.
Your name on a map doesn't buy you a drink. I've tried. The bastards just laughed.
My grandfather buried his savings in the garden. On a station. Nobody knows how. Still safer than our crap.
I've seen bigger hauls and smaller. This one's honest money, and honest money's rare as shit.
Ask me again when we've sold it, {to}. Until then it's numbers, and numbers can go to hell.

ivanova: {to}, when are we going to do some real mining again? I miss breaking things.
{to}, what is the best rock you ever cracked?
How are the mining tools, {to}? Rusting from boredom, like the rest of us?
{to}, is there any money left in rocks, or did someone mine it all before we got here?
{to}, painite or platinum? Settle this for me. The argument has gone on too long.
Do you miss the rings, {to}? The dust, the noise, the explosions?
{to}, what would it take to fit the ship for mining again? Honestly.
Have you ever had a charge go off wrong, {to}? Tell me the story. I like those stories.
{to}, deep core or laser? Which do you prefer, and why are you wrong?
Is mining as dull as it looks, or is it duller?
What is the most money you ever pulled out of one asteroid?
{to}, if we found a pristine ring out here, could you resist it?
ivanova_profane: {to}, when the hell are we blowing up rocks again? I miss the noise.
{to}, best damn rock you ever cracked? Go.
{to}, are the mining tools still aboard, or did the Commander chuck them for more fucking range?
Is there any money left in rocks, {to}, or did some bastard get there first?
{to}, painite or platinum? Settle it. This shit has gone on too long.
{to}, how many limpets have you got stashed? I know you've been hoarding the little bastards.
{to}, what would it take to refit for mining? Short answer. My patience is shot to hell.
Ever had a charge go off wrong, {to}? Tell me. I love a good disaster story.
Deep core or laser, {to}? Pick one, and then tell me why you're wrong as shit.
Is mining as dull as it looks, or is it even more fucking dull?
Biggest score you ever pulled out of one rock? Make me jealous.
{to}, if we found a pristine ring out here, could you resist it? Because I damn well couldn't.

ivanova: Mining is the only honest work there is, {to}. You hit the rock, the rock gives up. No arguments.
Rocks are like people, {to}. Hit them in the right place and they tell you everything.
The tools are fine. Oiled, packed, and waiting. Like a sword on the wall.
Painite, every time, {to}. Platinum is for people with no sense of drama.
Deep core is war. Lasers are farming. I am a soldier at heart.
This reminds me of when we mined the rings at Borann. So much ore the hold groaned. So much money I forgot to be bored.
If you find me a pristine ring, {to}, I will follow it like a dog follows a butcher.
I had a charge go off early once. The rock went one way, my eyebrows another. They grew back. Mostly.
Mining is patience with explosions at the end. The explosions make up for the patience.
There is still money in rocks, {to}. You just have to be willing to hit them harder than anyone else.
My grandfather mined ice on a moon of Lave. He said the rock always wins in the end. He was very cheerful.
No rings out here worth the trouble, as far as I have looked. When there is one, you will hear me.
ivanova_profane: Mining's the only job out here where you get to blow something up and nobody files a complaint, {to}. Fucking paradise.
Best rock I ever cracked split clean on the first charge. Prettiest damn thing I ever saw.
Platinum pays the bills, painite pays for the party, and I'm a shameless party animal, damn it.
Deep core charges, {to}. Drill, seed, run like hell, watch the bastard split. Best feeling there is.
Had a rock crack wrong once and spray fragments all over the canopy. Loudest I've ever sworn, and that's saying a shitload.
The tools are packed and waiting, {to}. Give me a decent ring and I'll show you how it's bloody done.
Laser mining is knitting with a hell of an electric bill.
We mined the ice rings in the Pleiades once, {to}, until a Thargoid showed up and ruined the whole damn afternoon.
My grandmother called asteroids God's piggy banks. Then she'd smash a real piggy bank to buy vodka. Crazy old saint.
There's money in rocks yet, {to}. Rocks don't run out. Patience runs out. Mine ran out years ago.
Give me a good ring and a hold full of limpets and I'm happy as a pig in shit.
Mining beats exploration, {to}. At least the rocks explode. These planets just sit there like assholes.

ivanova: {to}, any pirates brave enough to come out this far? I ask with hope.
{to}, what would you do if someone interdicted us right now? In detail, please.
How ready are the weapons, {to}? I would like to sleep tonight, eventually.
{to}, when did you last get to shoot at something? You seem restless.
{to}, are we safer out here than in the bubble, or just lonelier?
What worries you most out here, {to}? And do not say nothing. Everyone says nothing.
{to}, if a Thargoid showed up, what is the plan? Besides praying.
Do you ever miss the fighting, {to}? Honestly?
{to}, how long would our shields hold against a real attack? Ballpark.
Is it strange that I am disappointed nobody has tried to kill us lately?
Run or fight? If it came to it. Which would you choose?
{to}, tell me about the last good fight you had. I need a story with explosions.
ivanova_profane: {to}, any pirate bastards dumb enough to come out this far? God, I hope so.
{to}, someone interdicts us right now. What's the plan? Detail, damn it.
{to}, how ready are the guns? I want to know before some asshole tests them.
When did you last shoot something, {to}? You look twitchy as hell.
{to}, are we safer out here, or just bored out of our fucking minds?
What scares you out here, {to}? And don't you dare say nothing. Everybody says nothing, and it's crap.
{to}, a Thargoid drops in on us. Plan? Besides shitting ourselves.
Miss the fighting, {to}? I do. God, I bloody do.
{to}, how long do our shields last against something serious? Rough guess. Don't sugarcoat that shit.
Who's the nastiest pirate you ever tangled with? I want a name, so I can hunt the bastard down.
Run or fight, {to}? If it came to it. And if you say run, we're done talking.
{to}, tell me about your last good fight. I need a story with fucking explosions.

ivanova: Weapons are ready, {to}. They are always ready. That is the only thing I insist on.
Interdiction is just someone asking for a conversation. I prefer to answer with lasers.
Nobody has bothered us out here. It is very peaceful. I am bored out of my mind.
I would very much like to meet the next pirate who tries us, {to}. Briefly.
Thargoids are the only thing out here I respect, {to}. They are the only thing that does not bore me.
The trick with pirates is to be more frightening than they are. I practise in the mirror.
This reminds me of when we were interdicted outside Achenar. Three of them. The Commander would not let me shoot. I am still bitter.
My grandfather said if you want peace, prepare for war. Out here, I am prepared, and the peace is killing me.
Out here the danger is usually the planet, {to}, not the people. Planets do not negotiate.
Our shields are good. Our hull is good. Our luck I do not trust, but I never trust luck.
Whenever a ship passes, I imagine where I would put the first missile. It passes the time.
I keep the guns warm, {to}, the way other people keep a cat. It comforts me.
ivanova_profane: Guns are ready, {to}. They're always ready. The day they're not, somebody's getting their ass kicked, and it won't be the pirates.
Let them interdict us. I'll smile, let them get cocky, and then blow the bastards into next week.
Nobody's tried shit out here. It's peaceful as a church. I'm going out of my damn mind.
Thargoids? Different story, {to}. Those we run from, and I'll be swearing like hell the whole way.
Pirates out this far are either desperate or stupid, and both die the same way. Loudly.
Remember the Robigo run? Every station scan a knife fight. I've never felt more alive or more shit-scared.
Shields will hold long enough, {to}. That's all any sane soldier asks for, damn it.
The real danger out here is boredom. Boredom, and some cocky pilot getting too close to a fucking neutron star.
If we have to run, I'll run. I'll grumble the whole way, but I'll run.
I sleep with one hand on the trigger, {to}. Metaphorically. Mostly. Don't wake me suddenly.
I've got a speech ready for the next pirate. Three minutes of filthy language and one word at the end. Fire.
Chyort, {to}, I'd give a month's pay for one decent interdiction.

ivanova: {to}, heard anything on the comms lately besides static?
{to}, when did we last hear another commander's voice? I am starting to forget what people sound like.
Any good gossip from the stations, {to}? I will take bad gossip.
{to}, does anyone ever answer your hails out here?
{to}, what is the rudest thing a station controller ever said to you?
Are there other commanders out this way, {to}, or do we have the dark to ourselves?
{to}, what do you listen to on the long hauls? It cannot all be static.
Have you ever heard something on the comms you could not explain, {to}?
{to}, when we get back to the bubble, how loud will the traffic be? Prepare me.
Does the galaxy ever go quiet for you, or is there always someone talking?
Who was the worst pilot you ever talked down?
{to}, tell me something from the news. Anything. I am starving for news.
ivanova_profane: {to}, anything on the comms besides static and bullshit?
{to}, when did we last hear a voice that wasn't one of us? I'm going fucking stir crazy.
Got any gossip, {to}? Station drama, scandal, some bastard's love life, I don't care.
{to}, does anyone out here ever answer a damn hail?
Rudest thing a station controller ever said to you, {to}? Bet I can beat it.
{to}, are there other commanders out this way, or have we got this shithole to ourselves?
{to}, what the hell do you listen to on the long hauls?
Ever hear something on the comms you couldn't explain, {to}? Something creepy as shit?
{to}, back in the bubble, how loud's the traffic going to be? Give me time to brace, damn it.
Does it ever go quiet for you, or is some idiot always yapping?
Worst pilot you ever had to talk down, {to}? Name and shame. I fucking love that.
Give me news, {to}. Any news. I'm starving for it like a damn prisoner.

ivanova: Static, mostly, {to}. Static and the occasional beacon reciting its name like a lonely child.
Out here nobody answers. I hail anyway. It is a habit, like praying.
Station controllers are like grandmothers. Always disappointed, always right about the landing gear.
This reminds me of when we docked at Abraham Lincoln. So much traffic, so many speeches over the comms. I have never wanted silence so badly.
Other commanders pass now and then, {to}. They wave, we wave, everyone goes home lonely.
I keep a list of every voice I hear out here. It is a short list. I read it sometimes, like poetry.
I picked up a distress beacon once that had been calling for three hundred years. Nobody came. I listened to it for an hour, out of respect.
When we go home, there will be a thousand voices on every channel. For now, there is the hum, and that is enough.
The galaxy is never quiet, {to}. It just stops talking to us for a while.
Busy stations sound like a wedding where everyone is the angry uncle.
News reaches us late out here, {to}. By the time we hear about a war, it is probably over. I find that restful.
Da, I could hail someone, {to}. But who would I hail? The nearest person is very far, and probably asleep.
ivanova_profane: Nothing but static, {to}. Hours of fucking static. I've started naming the crackles.
I hail anyway. Out of spite. Somebody out there owes me a damn conversation.
A Jameson Memorial controller once told me to park better. I parked perfectly. I'm still pissed about it.
Ever tried flying into Sol without a permit? The Navy is very polite while it threatens to blow you to hell.
Other commanders? Out here? Once in a blue moon, and they never want to chat. Antisocial bastards. My people.
Old broadcasts bounce around out here for centuries, {to}. Ancient adverts. Terrible damn music. I love every second.
Heard singing on the comms once, way out past the Pleiades. Didn't stay to find out what. Creepiest shit of my life.
Back in the bubble it'll be assholes shouting docking requests on every channel. I'll miss this. Don't tell anyone, {to}.
Station traffic is a fish market with lasers, {to}. Everybody yelling, nobody listening, and somebody always fucking crashes.
News? Some faction's pissed at another faction. It's always that. Always the same crap.
The comms are quiet, so I talk to myself. I'm better company than most of the bastards I used to talk to.
Comms is a lot of listening to nothing, {to}. I'd kill for a good insult on an open channel. Hell, I'd settle for a bad one.

ivanova: {to}, what do you honestly make of the Commander's flying?
{to}, does the Commander ever ask your advice, or just pretend to?
Is the Commander as calm as they look, {to}? Nobody is that calm.
{to}, what was the Commander's worst landing? I need it for my memoirs.
{to}, why does the Commander keep heading further out? Is there something they are not telling us?
Do you trust the Commander's decisions, {to}? Every one? Even the strange ones?
{to}, has the Commander ever ignored your advice and been right? That would annoy me.
{to}, how would you describe the Commander in one word? A polite word, please.
Does the Commander ever sleep, {to}? I have not seen it happen.
What would the Commander do in a real fight? I have only seen exploring.
Is the Commander enjoying this, do you think? Because I have stopped being able to tell.
{to}, between us. Is the Commander brave, or just stubborn?
ivanova_profane: {to}, what do you really make of the Commander's flying? Honestly. No bullshit.
{to}, does the Commander ever listen to you, or just nod and do whatever the hell they want?
{to}, what's the Commander's worst habit? Spill it. I've got some good shit to trade.
{to}, worst landing the Commander ever pulled? I want every damn detail.
Why does the Commander keep pushing further out, {to}? What's out there that's worth all this crap?
{to}, do you trust every call the Commander makes? Even the weird shit?
{to}, has the Commander ever ignored your advice and turned out right? That'd piss me off for a week.
One word for the Commander, {to}. Go. And you're allowed to swear.
Does the Commander ever sleep, {to}? I've never once seen it. Creepy as hell.
What's the Commander like in a real fight? All I've seen is the scenic damn tour.
{to}, between us. Brave, or just stubborn as a bastard?
Is the Commander actually enjoying this, {to}? I've lost the ability to tell, and it's freaking me the fuck out.

ivanova: The Commander flies like someone with nothing to prove and something to find. I respect it. Mostly.
They ask my opinion, {to}, wait politely, and then do the thing. I have learned to enjoy the ritual.
The Commander is right more often than I would like. I keep a list. It is a long list, and I hate it.
Their worst landing? I promised never to tell. I did not promise never to hint. There was a lot of smoke.
The Commander heads further out because the Commander is curious. I head further out because I signed a contract.
Calm? Yes. Like a frozen lake, {to}. You do not know what is underneath until you fall in.
I trust the Commander with my life. My patience, less so.
This reminds me of when we hauled passengers out of Sothis and the Commander took the long way to see a nebula. The passengers complained. I secretly agreed with the Commander.
Brave or stubborn? Out here it is the same thing, {to}. The difference is whether you come home.
The Commander rarely asks my advice, and takes it about half the time. For a commander, that is practically worship.
My grandmother would have liked the Commander. She liked anyone who argued with her and won.
The Commander is a good pilot, {to}. Do not tell them I said so. I have a reputation for grumbling.
ivanova_profane: The Commander flies like a lunatic with a plan. Scares the shit out of me. I'd follow them anywhere.
They hear me out, {to}. Every word. Then they do what they damn well planned. Infuriating, and usually right.
The Commander's got instincts I'd kill for. Nine times out of ten they're right, and the tenth time is fucking spectacular.
Worst landing? Ask the pad at Hutton Orbital. Actually, don't. It's still pissed off.
Why does the Commander keep going further? Because the bubble's full of politics and bullshit, and out here there's just the work.
Calm, {to}? Sure. The kind of calm that makes pirates nervous as hell. I love it.
I trust the Commander with my life. With the music aboard, not a fucking chance.
Remember the Commander threading the slot at Jameson Memorial at full boost? I nearly lost my lunch. They grinned like a damn child.
Is the Commander brave? {to}, you have to be brave or barking mad to fly out here. Probably both, and so am I, God help me.
The Commander never panics. I panic enough for both of us, out loud, with swearing. It's a damn good system.
Between you and me, {to}, the Commander's the best pilot I've ever flown with. Tell anyone and I'll kill you, and I won't make it quick.
If the Commander ever retires, I'll have to find someone else to grumble at. Hell, I'd miss it.

ivanova: {to}, how do you keep from losing your mind on a quiet watch?
{to}, how long have we been sitting here? It feels like a week.
What do you do when nothing is happening, {to}? I need new ideas. I have run out.
{to}, is it just me, or does time slow down out here?
Do you ever count the stars on watch, {to}? I tried. I gave up at four hundred and got angry.
{to}, what is the most boring watch you ever stood?
{to}, talk to me. About anything. The silence is starting to talk back.
Do you ever sleep on watch, {to}? I will not tell. Probably.
{to}, if nothing happens in the next hour, will you promise to shoot me?
How do you pass the time? And do not say reading. Nobody reads.
Is a quiet watch a gift or a punishment? I can never decide.
{to}, play a game with me. Any game. I am dying of boredom here.
ivanova_profane: {to}, how the hell do you stay sane on a watch this quiet?
{to}, what's your record for not screaming on watch? Mine's about to end, damn it.
{to}, what do you do when nothing's happening? Because I'm out of ideas and losing my shit.
Is it just me, {to}, or does time crawl on its belly out here, damn it?
{to}, ever count the stars on watch? I gave up at four hundred and wanted to punch something.
Most boring watch you ever stood, {to}? Bet this shit beats it.
{to}, tell me a joke. A filthy one. I don't care how shit it is.
Ever nap on watch, {to}? I won't tell. Probably. Hell, I might join you.
{to}, if nothing happens in the next hour, put me out of my damn misery.
Does anyone actually like the quiet watches, or are we all lying through our fucking teeth?
Is a quiet watch a gift or a punishment, {to}? Feels like bloody punishment to me.
{to}, play a game with me. Anything. I'm bored as shit over here.

ivanova: I count things. Rivets, stars, regrets. The rivets are the shortest list.
Time does slow down out here, {to}. I have measured it. Scientifically. By being bored.
My grandmother used to knit through every long winter. I tried knitting on watch once. The needles are now in the recycler.
A quiet watch is a gift, {to}. I just wish it came with a receipt so I could return it.
I make plans. Detailed plans. For fights that never come. I win every one of them.
This reminds me of when we sat in the queue outside Jameson Memorial for an hour. I aged. I sulked. I learned nothing.
Do not ask me how long we have been out here. I stopped counting when counting made me sad.
I talk to the ship. The ship does not answer, which makes it the best listener aboard, {to}.
Silence is fine. Silence means nobody is shooting. I hate that it means nobody is shooting.
I recite old poems in my head. Russian ones. Very long, very sad. They make the watch feel short by comparison.
Nothing is happening, {to}, and I am at peace with it. That is a lie. I am not at peace with anything.
My secret? I pretend every star is an enemy and we are sneaking past it. So far we are winning.
ivanova_profane: I sharpen things, {to}. Knives, comebacks, grudges. Mostly grudges.
I do push-ups until my arms quit, then I swear at the stars until they quit. They never fucking quit.
Long watches are when I write my memoirs in my head. Chapter one, Bored As Shit. Chapter two, Still Bored.
Time doesn't pass out here, {to}. It just sits on your chest like a fat damn cat.
When it's this quiet I start hearing things in the hull. Then I realise it's me grinding my bloody teeth.
I rearrange my locker. Again. It's the most organised locker in the whole damn fleet.
Quiet means nobody's shooting, {to}. I'm trying to see that as a good thing. It's not fucking working.
On the Sothis runs we did watches so long I learned to sleep with my eyes open. Hell of a skill.
My grandmother used to say a watched pot never boils. Well, I'm watching the whole galaxy and not a damn thing's boiling.
Give it time, {to}. Something always goes to shit eventually. That's what keeps me going.
I play chess against myself. I cheat. I still lose. Bastard.
The trick is to find one small thing to hate, {to}, and hate it properly. Today it's that crappy blinking light.

ivanova: {to}, tell me about your family. And do not say they were normal. Nobody's family is normal.
So, {to}. Brothers, sisters, a mad aunt? What was your family like?
{to}, who raised you? I want to know who to blame.
What were your people like, {to}? Loud, quiet, dangerous?
Family. Everyone has one, even out here. What was yours like?
{to}, did your family ever sit down to dinner together, or did they fight like mine?
{to}, I am curious. Who was the troublemaker in your family? Was it you?
Tell me something about your family, {to}. Something they would not want me to know.
I always wonder who people come from. Who did you come from, {to}?
Does your family know where you are right now, {to}? Do they approve?
Did anyone in your family fly, or are you the black sheep?
{to}, what would your family say if they saw you on this ship?
ivanova_profane: {to}, family. Spill it. And spare me the happy holo-card crap.
Who the hell raised you, {to}? I have questions for them.
{to}, brothers, sisters, some mad bastard of an uncle? Give me the whole cast.
What sort of people made you, {to}? The loud kind or the dangerous kind?
Everyone out in this godforsaken dark came from somewhere. What was your family like?
{to}, did your lot eat together, or did dinner end in shouting like mine? Mine always did, damn it.
Be honest, {to}. Who was the family troublemaker? It was you. I know it was you.
{to}, give me something embarrassing about your family. Something they would kill you for telling.
Saints or sinners, {to}? Your family, I mean. And do not bullshit me.
{to}, does anyone back home know where the hell you are right now?
Anyone in your family fly, or are you the one damn black sheep?
If your family could see you on this bucket, {to}, what would they say? Brutally honest, please.

ivanova: My family? Loud, {to}. Very loud. Dinner was a battle, and my grandmother always won.
My grandmother had a saying for everything. Trouble never comes alone, she said, usually while handing you more trouble.
My mother ran station security. She could stop a riot with one look. She still uses that look on me.
My father fixed reactors and said perhaps ten words a year, {to}. Most of them were about spanners.
I have an older brother, a navy pilot. He taught me to fly, and then I beat him. He has not forgiven me.
My grandfather flew patrol for forty years and told stories about all of it. Half of them were true. He never said which half.
We were a family of fighters, {to}. Not the kind with fists. Well. Sometimes the kind with fists.
Why do you ask, {to}? Ha. All right. Strict mother, silent father, a babushka who could curse in three languages, and a brother who is still annoying.
My grandmother used to say, if you want peace, prepare for war. Then she would cut the bread like it owed her money.
There was always someone shouting in our home. When it went quiet, that was when you worried.
They are all still back there, {to}, arguing about whose turn it is to call me. Nobody ever calls.
My family taught me two things: never trust a quiet room, and always finish your soup.
ivanova_profane: Loud as hell, {to}. Every dinner a war, and Grandmother never lost a single battle.
Grandmother had a proverb for every disaster. Trouble never comes alone, she would say, then dump another damn bucket of it in your lap.
My mother ran security on our station. One look from her and rioters went home to bed. That look still scares the shit out of me.
My father, {to}? Reactor technician. Ten words a year, and nine of them were swearing at the fucking reactor.
Big brother flies for the navy. Taught me everything, then I outflew him inside a year. The bastard still sulks about it.
Grandfather flew patrol for forty years and turned every one of them into glorious bullshit. I believed all of it.
We fought, {to}. Mostly with words. Sometimes with chairs. Damn good chairs, too, built to last.
Strict mother, silent father, a grandmother who cursed like a docking pilot, and a brother who is still a pain in my ass. That is the whole circus, {to}.
If you want peace, prepare for war. Grandmother said it every morning, then attacked the bread like it had insulted her. Scary as hell.
Someone was always yelling at our place. When it went quiet, you knew the shit was coming.
They are all back home, {to}, fighting over whose turn it is to call me. Nobody ever bloody calls.
The family rules: never trust a quiet room, and finish your soup, or God help you.

{to}, what was the place you grew up like? Busy, quiet, dangerous?
Planet or station, {to}? Where were you a child?
What is the first place you remember?
{to}, do you ever miss where you grew up, or did you get out the first chance you had?
Tell me about home, {to}. The real home, not the one on your papers.
{to}, if I went to where you grew up, what would I find there?
Where did you learn to be like this, {to}? Which corner of the galaxy made you?
Is there a place you still call home?
{to}, what did home smell like? Mine smelled of recycled air and cabbage.
{to}, could you go back to where you grew up, if you wanted to?
ivanova_profane: {to}, where the hell did you grow up? Tell me there was sunshine. Somebody here deserves to have had sunshine.
Is this damn ship your home now, {to}, or is there somewhere else?
{to}, the place you grew up. Nice and quiet, or a total shithole?
Station kid or planet kid, {to}? Where did they let you loose?
First place you remember. Go. Do not think about it.
{to}, do you miss home, or did you get the fuck out the first chance you had?
{to}, the real home. Not the crap they put on your papers.
If I turned up where you grew up, {to}, what would I find? Besides people with stories about you.
Which corner of the galaxy made you like this, {to}? I want to send them a bill.
Anywhere you still call home, or is that sentimental bullshit to you?
{to}, what did home smell like? Mine was recycled air and bloody cabbage, every day of my childhood.
{to}, could you go back home if you wanted to? Would they even let you in?

ivanova: I grew up on a mining station over an ice moon, {to}. Cold corridors, recycled air, and everyone knew your business.
A station. Small, old, and always one broken pump from disaster. It made me who I am. Grim, mostly.
We lived three decks above the docking bay. I fell asleep to ships landing. I still sleep badly anywhere quiet.
Home was a ring station in a system nobody has heard of. I will not tell you the name, {to}. You would only try to visit.
The station had one window big enough to see the moon. Every child fought over it. I usually won.
I learned to fly in the traffic lanes outside our station. The traffic controllers knew me by name. Not fondly.
Cold, {to}. Home was cold. Even in summer, and there was no summer.
Our deck had a bakery, a bar, and a security office. Between them, they raised me.
I left home at seventeen and swore I would never miss it. I lied. Do not tell anyone.
Where I grew up, if the alarms went off, nobody panicked. Everyone just reached for a helmet and kept eating.
My grandmother called our station the tin can at the end of the world. She said it with love. Some love.
Home? Corridors, {to}. Endless grey corridors. That is why I like a cockpit. At least it has a view.
ivanova_profane: An ice-mining station, {to}, hanging over a frozen moon. Cold as hell, air like old socks, and everybody in your damn business.
Old, cramped, and one busted pump away from killing us all. Built character. Shitty character, but character.
Our quarters sat right over the docking bay, ships coming in all night. Now I cannot sleep anywhere this fucking quiet.
A ring station nobody has heard of, {to}. You do not want the name. You would go, and it is a dump.
One window on the whole deck looked out on the moon, and every kid fought over it. I fought dirty. I won, damn it.
Taught myself to fly in the lanes outside home. Traffic control knew me as that little shit again.
Bloody cold, {to}. Every season. Not that we had seasons.
A bakery, a bar and a security office, all on one deck. Between them they raised me. The bar did the most damage.
Left at seventeen. Swore I would never miss it. Turns out I am a goddamn liar.
Alarms went off back home and nobody even looked up. You grabbed a helmet and finished your dinner.
Grandmother called it the tin can at the arse end of the world. With love. Mostly.
Corridors, {to}. Grey, endless, mind-numbing corridors. Give me a cockpit over that crap any day.

ivanova: {to}, what is the best thing you have ever eaten? And do not say ration bars.
Best meal of your life, {to}. Go. I need something to dream about.
{to}, what is the worst thing anyone ever fed you?
If you could eat anything right now, {to}, what would it be?
What did your family cook, back home?
{to}, have you ever eaten something so bad you still remember it?
{to}, tell me about a meal worth remembering. Good or terrible, I do not care.
Which station has the best food you have ever had, {to}? I am planning ahead.
What is the one dish you would cross the galaxy for?
{to}, be honest. What is the strangest thing you have ever eaten on purpose?
{to}, sweet or savoury? And what is the best of it you ever had?
Do you remember a meal that made everything better, {to}?
ivanova_profane: {to}, best thing you ever ate. If you say ration bars, I will put you out the airlock myself.
I need something to dream about, {to}. Give me the best damn meal of your life.
{to}, what is the shittiest thing anyone ever fed you?
Right now, {to}, anything in the galaxy on a plate. What the hell are you having?
What did they cook where you grew up? Anything better than this galley crap?
{to}, ever eaten something so fucking bad you can still taste it?
{to}, one meal you will never forget. Wonderful or bloody awful, either will do.
{to}, which station serves the best food? I am planning my escape.
Name the one dish you would cross this whole damn galaxy for.
Strangest thing you ever ate on purpose, {to}. No holding back.
{to}, sweet or savoury? And the best of it, the kind that made you swear out loud?
Ever had a meal that made all the shit in your life go away for an hour, {to}?

ivanova: My grandmother's dumplings, {to}. Pelmeni, folded by hand, a hundred at a time. Nothing in the galaxy comes close.
Best meal? Soup, on a cold night, after a twelve hour shift. Any soup. Hunger is the best cook.
The worst was a navy canteen stroganoff. Synthetic beef, synthetic cream, real regret. I still dream about it. Badly.
There was a sandwich at Hutton Orbital, {to}. I paid a fortune for it after that endless trip. It was stale. I ate it anyway, weeping.
My grandmother's borscht. Red as a warning light and twice as dangerous. I miss it every day.
The best meal I ever had was after my first real fight. Cold noodles in a hangar. I have never tasted anything better.
On Jameson Memorial there is a little place by the docks that does a steak worth dying for, {to}. I nearly did. Long story.
The worst? Something a trader sold me as fish. It was not fish. It may not have been food.
Black bread and salt, {to}, the way my grandfather ate it. Simple. Honest. Like a good punch.
I once ate a Fuel Rat's emergency ration bar out of gratitude. Gratitude has limits. That bar found them.
Honestly? Whatever is hot, as long as nobody is shooting at me while I eat it. That is luxury.
My mother made one cake a year, on my birthday. It was always slightly burnt. It was always perfect.
ivanova_profane: Grandmother's pelmeni, {to}. Folded by hand, a hundred at a sitting, and nothing in this whole damn galaxy comes close.
Hot soup after a double shift in a freezing hangar. When you are that hungry, even the crap tastes like heaven.
Worst ever: a navy canteen stroganoff. Fake beef, fake cream, real fucking regret.
Hutton Orbital, {to}. Hours of supercruise, a fortune in credits for one sandwich, and the bastard thing was stale.
Grandmother's borscht. Red as a warning light, and it could strip paint. God, I miss it like hell.
Cold noodles on a hangar floor after my first real fight. Best damn thing I ever ate. Adrenaline is a hell of a sauce.
A little place by the docks on Jameson Memorial, {to}. A steak worth dying for. I nearly did. It is a shitty story, do not ask.
The worst? Something a trader swore was fish. It was not fish. I am not sure it was even dead.
Black bread and salt, {to}, the way my grandfather ate it. No frills, no bullshit.
I ate a Fuel Rats ration bar once, out of gratitude. Gratitude only goes so far. It tasted like a boot full of piss.
Anything hot I can eat without some asshole shooting at me. That is luxury.
One cake a year, my mother made, for my birthday. Always a bit burnt. Always bloody perfect.

ivanova: {to}, what is the best day you can remember? I need cheering up.
Best day of your life, {to}. Tell me about it. Make it good.
{to}, was there ever a day when everything went right?
If you could live one day over again, {to}, which would it be?
What is the happiest you have ever been? I will not laugh. Probably.
{to}, tell me about a day you would not trade for anything.
{to}, when was the last time you were really, truly happy?
Go on, {to}. Your best day. I promise not to make it about me.
Is there a day you still think about? The good kind.
{to}, what day made you think, this is why I live?
{to}, a perfect day. Have you had one? What happened?
Tell me the best day you ever had, {to}, and I will tell you mine. Mine involves explosions.
ivanova_profane: Cheer me the hell up, {to}. What is the best day you can remember?
{to}, your best day ever. Spill it, and make it bloody good.
{to}, ever had a day when not one damn thing went wrong?
One day to live again, {to}. Which one do you pick?
Happiest you have ever been? I will not laugh. Much. Shit, I might.
{to}, a day you would not trade for all the credits in the fucking galaxy. Go.
When were you last truly happy, {to}? Not this crap. Really happy.
Go on, {to}. Best day. I swear I will not turn it into a story about me.
Is there a good day you still replay, {to}? The good kind, damn it, not the sad kind.
{to}, what day made you think, this is why I put up with all this shit?
{to}, ever had a perfect day? Tell me. I want to be jealous.
Trade you, {to}. Your best day for mine. Fair warning, mine has big explosions in it.

ivanova: My first patrol, {to}. A pirate wing jumped us, and every one of our ships came home. Three of theirs did not. Best day of my life.
A close second: my first solo flight. My brother watched from the tower, waiting for me to crash. I did not. His face was worth a fortune.
The day my grandmother laughed at one of my jokes. She laughed maybe twice in her life. I was there for one.
The day I got the keys to my first ship, {to}. Second hand, ugly, and mine. I sat in the cockpit for an hour doing nothing, and I was happy. It did not last.
The day they gave me my own traffic tower. That same afternoon someone attacked the station. Command and a fight on the same day. Perfect.
Honestly, {to}? Any day something explodes and it is not us. But my first kill on that first patrol stands out. I still remember the light.
The night we won the station's flying race. Old ship, bad engine, and I beat every one of them. My grandfather cried. He denied it.
Perfect days are dangerous, {to}. You start expecting them. But yes, my first patrol. Everything went right. I have been suspicious ever since.
There was a sunrise on a moon once, on shore leave. No alarms, no orders, nothing to shoot. I hated how much I liked it.
The day I left home with a pilot's licence in my pocket and nobody to answer to. Terrifying. Wonderful.
I do not have many. But the first time I outflew my brother in a mock dogfight, the whole squadron watched. Glorious.
A best day? Every day nothing goes wrong is a good day. The best ones, something goes wrong and I fix it with a gun.
ivanova_profane: First patrol, {to}. A pirate wing jumped us. All our ships made it home, three of theirs did not. Best damn day of my life.
Close second: my first solo. My brother up in the tower, waiting for me to pile it in. I did not. The look on his smug fucking face.
Grandmother laughed at one of my jokes once. Maybe the second laugh of her whole life. Hell of an honour.
The day I got my first ship, {to}. Second hand, ugly as hell, and all mine. Sat in the cockpit for an hour doing fuck all, grinning like an idiot.
They handed me my own traffic tower, and that same afternoon some idiot attacked the station. Command and a fight in one day. Fucking perfect.
Honestly, {to}? Any day something blows up and it is not us. But my first kill on patrol, shit, I still see that flash.
We won the station flying race in a ship held together with tape and spite. Grandfather cried like hell. Denied it, of course.
You start expecting perfect days, {to}, and they stop coming. But that first patrol, damn. Suspicious of good luck ever since.
Shore leave, a sunrise on some moon, nothing to shoot and nobody giving orders. I hated how much I liked it.
Walking out of home with a fresh pilot's licence and nobody to answer to. Scared shitless. Never been happier.
Beating my brother in a mock dogfight, the whole squadron watching. He calls it a fluke. It was not a fucking fluke.
Any day nothing goes wrong is a good day. The best ones, something goes to hell and I sort it out with a gun.

{to}, would a fortune change you, do you think?

{to}, a billion credits, no strings. First damn thing you buy?
{to}, with a fortune in the bank, would you still be out in this crap?
More money than sense, {to}. Go. Some of us have already fucked up the sense part.

{to}, one purchase, any size. Ship, house, whole bloody planet?
{to}, would a fortune turn you into an arsehole, do you think? Be honest.
Sensible or fun as hell, {to}? Tell me what you would do with a fortune and I will decide.

{to}, a mountain of credits drops on you. Blow it, or bury it?
{to}, what would you buy that you would never admit to wanting? I will not tell. Much.
Rich as sin, {to}. Who the hell gets a share?

ivanova: A warship, {to}. Something big, ugly and armed to the teeth. And then I would go looking for pirates on purpose.
I would buy my grandmother a house on a real planet, with a garden and a real sky. She would complain about the weather. Happily.
A bar on Jameson Memorial. Small, dark, good music. Pilots would tell their stories, and I would tell them they were wrong.
First, I would never scan another rock. Second, I would pay someone to scan rocks for me, so I can watch them suffer.
I would pay off my father's station debts, {to}. He would never say thank you. He would fix my ship for free forever instead.
A fortune? Ammunition. A great deal of ammunition.
My grandfather said money is like water in a sieve. I would test that. Thoroughly.
Honestly, {to}? I would buy the fastest combat ship I could find and race my brother until he begged for mercy.
I would hire a crew to do all the waiting for me. Then I would show up for the shooting.
Nothing sensible. Sensible is for people with no money.
Some of it I would give away, {to}. Quietly. My family never had much, and somebody always helped. The rest goes on guns.
A fortune does not last, {to}. Trouble never comes alone, and neither do the tax collectors. So spend it fast.
ivanova_profane: A warship, {to}. Big, ugly, armed to the fucking teeth. Then I go hunting pirates for fun.
A house on a real planet for my grandmother, garden and all. She would bitch about the weather every day and love every minute.
My own little bar on Jameson Memorial. Pilots tell me their war stories and I tell them they are full of shit.
Step one, I never scan another damn rock. Step two, I hire some poor soul to scan them while I watch.
Clear my father's station debts, {to}. He would never say thank you, the stubborn bastard. He would just keep my ship running forever.
A fortune? Ammunition. A hell of a lot of ammunition.
Money runs through your fingers like water, Grandfather said. Good. I would like to drown in it, gloriously.
Honestly, {to}? The fastest combat ship money can buy, and I race my brother until he cries. Hell, until he quits flying.
Hire a crew to do all the waiting. I turn up for the shooting and nothing else. Fuck the waiting.
Nothing sensible, that is for damn sure. Sensible is for broke people.
A share goes to people who need it, {to}. Quietly. We never had much and somebody always helped. The rest goes on guns, obviously.
Fortunes never last, {to}. Trouble never comes alone, and the tax collectors come in bloody packs. Spend it fast.

ivanova: System security, {to}. Wing patrols, pirate hunting, real work. Then they promoted me to a desk.
I ran the traffic tower at a busy station. Four thousand ships a day, every one of them in a hurry and every one of them wrong.
Before this? I flew patrols. Then I ran docking control. Then I got bored and signed on here, for excitement. Yes. I know.
Traffic control, {to}. You have never heard real shouting until a trader tries to dock on the wrong pad in the middle of a convoy.
I was a security pilot for years. Good years. Lots of explosions. I still miss the explosions.
I sat in a tower telling pilots no, {to}. Hundreds of times a day. I was very good at it. I still am.
They said this ship would be an adventure. They did not say it would be an adventure in patience.
My last posting was a station with a pirate problem. Then the pirates stopped coming, and I was bored within a week.
I spent a few years escorting convoys, {to}. Slow ships, nervous traders, and now and then someone foolish enough to try them. I miss the foolish ones.
I worked station traffic, {to}. Think of it as herding cats, if the cats were armed and late.
I trained new pilots for a while. Most of them were terrified of me. The rest were wrong.
What did I do? I kept people alive, mostly by yelling at them. It is a skill. I still practise.
ivanova_profane: System security, {to}. Wing patrols, pirate hunting, real fucking work. Then some genius promoted me to a desk.
Ran the tower at a big station. Thousands of ships a day, every pilot in a hurry, every damn one of them wrong.
Patrols, then docking control, then I got bored and signed on here for the excitement. Yes. I know. Do not say it.
Traffic control, {to}. Picture a trader trying to dock on the wrong pad in the middle of a convoy. Holy shit, the noise.
Security pilot, years of it. Explosions every week. Damn, I miss the explosions.
Telling pilots no from a tower, {to}, hundreds of times a day. Fuck, I was good at it.
Adventure, they told me when I signed on. Nobody said the adventure was sitting on my ass.
Last posting had a pirate problem. Then the pirates stopped coming and I was bored as hell inside a week.
Convoy escort for a few years, {to}. Slow ships, twitchy traders, and every so often some bastard dumb enough to have a go. I miss the dumb bastards.
Station traffic, {to}. Herding cats, if the cats were armed, late and pissed off.
Trained new pilots for a while. Most were terrified of me. The rest were idiots. Some were both, God bless them.
Keeping people alive by yelling at them, mostly. Bloody effective, too.
